headline: Graph and language-model embeddings infer unmeasured RNA, protein and drug interactions
label: Biological Interaction Inference Models
summary: Pretrained RNA and protein language-model embeddings are now paired with graph and state-space architectures for interaction prediction across several…
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of biological relations that are not directly observed, using graph-structured or sequence-derived representations in place of measured contact. CrossLLM-Mamba fuses ESM-2 and RiNALMo embeddings through bidirectional Mamba state-space encoders to predict RNA-protein, RNA-small molecule and RNA-RNA interactions. The multiplex framework targets zero-shot interaction prediction in multiplex biological networks by combining foundation-model embeddings with topology-aware modeling. BioGraphX-RNA fuses frozen RiNALMo embeddings with physicochemical interaction graphs for RNA subcellular localization, and GRASP applies a heterogeneous graph neural network to the same problem using multi-scale substructures. RCLG-PPIS couples an EGNN with a transformer for protein-protein interaction sites, and DVMMHGNN applies contrastive heterogeneous graph learning to drug-disease associations. GraSPNet, a fragment-based self-supervised framework, addresses molecular representation rather than interaction prediction. What is new is the explicit emphasis on zero-shot generalization to unseen interactions alongside pretrained embeddings, rather than multimodal fusion alone.
